text: No, we cannot confidently state that the asset is affected by deforestation or non–EUDR compliant based on this evidence. While tree-cover loss totaling 86.4 ha occurred after the 2020 baseline (primarily 81.3 ha in 2021), the data does not confirm whether this was deforestation, as the losses mainly occurred in planted forests (not primary/natural forests). EUDR compliance requires illegal deforestation or conversion of natural ecosystems, but the evidence does not establish legality, intention, or ecosystem type. The losses could reflect legal harvesting, regeneration cuts, or other non-deforestation activities. Further ground data or higher-resolution analysis would be needed to assess EUDR compliance.
